### Summary

When a root `HTTPProxy` delegates a path prefix to a child `HTTPProxy`, the child can use a regex condition to match paths outside that prefix. It can then receive requests that are meant for other routes in the same virtual host.

### Details

The regex for a child route is built by combining the root prefix from `spec.includes[].conditions[].prefix` with the child regex from `spec.routes[].conditions[].regex`. The child can use alternation `|` in the regex to match paths outside the root prefix.

### Proof of concept

Root `HTTPProxy` sends `/admin` to service `admin`, and includes child `HTTPProxy` `team-a/app` with prefix `/team-a`:

```yaml
apiVersion: projectcontour.io/v1
kind: HTTPProxy
metadata:
  name: main
  namespace: admin
spec:
  virtualhost:
    fqdn: app.example.com
  routes:
  - conditions:
    - prefix: /admin
    services:
    - name: admin
      port: 80
  includes:
  - name: app
    namespace: team-a
    conditions:
    - prefix: /team-a
```

Child `HTTPProxy` `app` uses a regex with `|`:

```yaml
apiVersion: projectcontour.io/v1
kind: HTTPProxy
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  routes:
  - conditions:
    - regex: /x|/admin/.*
    services:
    - name: app
      port: 80
```

Contour combines the root prefix `/team-a` and the child regex `/x|/admin/.*` into the regex match `^/team-a/x|/admin/.*`. This wrongly also matches every path that starts with `/admin/`, and as a result, requests to `http://app.example.com/admin/login` go to service `app` in namespace `team-a` instead of service `admin` in namespace `admin`.

To list the regex conditions of all HTTPProxies:

```
kubectl get httpproxy -A -o custom-columns='NAMESPACE:.metadata.namespace,NAME:.metadata.name,FQDN:.spec.virtualhost.fqdn,REGEX:.spec.routes[*].conditions[*].regex'
```

If an HTTPProxy without FQDN has `|` in its regex, check that the regex cannot match paths outside the root prefix.

### Impact

Users who can create a child `HTTPProxy` can receive requests intended for other paths on different HTTPProxies within the same virtual host.
